sources.title: Analytic and Expressive Communication Immersion — actual philosophy/ethics course cards
sources.locator: Current curriculum table and complete settled public popup opened from the exact course-code link.

scope: Thirty-seven complete public course popups; manual interpretation separate from observations. No prerequisite-chain expansion or identity merging.

PHIL-201.name: Ancient Philosophy
PHIL-201.description: Examines Greek philosophical traditions and their questions about knowledge, language, reality, nature and ethical life.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was present; null does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.rationale: Historical interpretation of philosophical ideas and ethical questions is central.

PHIL-202.name: Foundations of Moral Philosophy
PHIL-202.description: Surveys virtue ethics, deontology, consequentialism and questions about moral obligations, judgment and worthwhile life.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was present; null does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.rationale: The description explicitly centers normative moral reasoning rather than a technical method.

PHIL-203.name: Modern Philosophy
PHIL-203.description: Traces philosophy from Descartes through Kant, examining knowledge, mind/body relations, causation, reality and religion.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was present; null does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.rationale: The course interprets the history of thought and conceptual questions; references to science do not establish scientific-method instruction.

PHIL-205.name: Symbolic Logic
PHIL-205.description: Teaches propositional and first-order predicate logic through truth tables, truth trees and formal derivations.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was present; null does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.rationale: Formal deductive systems and proof techniques establish mathematics; no programming or AI implementation is described.

PHIL-301.name: Philosophy of Religion
PHIL-301.description: Critically examines religious definitions, assumptions and arguments, including divinity, evil, religious language and experience.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was present; null does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.rationale: The stated methods are philosophical interpretation and argument about religion.

PHIL-303.name: Philosophy of Art/Aesthetics
PHIL-303.description: Examines art and aesthetic experience in relation to morality, ugliness, truth and other human experience.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was present; null does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.rationale: The inquiry is philosophical interpretation of art, rather than artistic production.

PHIL-304.name: Philosophy of Law
PHIL-304.description: Studies the justification of law, legal thought, justice and relations among law, ethics and morality.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was present; null does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.rationale: Legal and ethical interpretation directly supports human context.

PHIL-305.name: Philosophy of Peace
PHIL-305.description: Examines just peace, national interests, force, violence and the ethics of peacemaking institutions.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was present; null does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.rationale: The substantive work is normative analysis of social and international relations.

PHIL-306.name: Professional Ethics
PHIL-306.description: Critically examines ethical problems in professional life and their consequences across different professions.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was present; null does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.rationale: Professional practice is the setting for ethical analysis, not training in a particular occupational technique.

PHIL-308.name: Environmental Philosophy
PHIL-308.description: Evaluates environmental values and ethical theories through conservation, climate, sustainability and environmental-justice cases.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was present; null does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.rationale: The course centers ethics, metaphysics and policy values rather than ecological measurement or environmental engineering.

PHIL-309.name: Feminist Theory
PHIL-309.description: Examines feminist thought, sex and gender, identity, knowledge production, embodiment and ethical decision making.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was present; null does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.rationale: The stated objectives concern cultural categories and social/ethical interpretation.

PHIL-310.name: Knowledge and Truth
PHIL-310.description: Compares theories of knowledge and truth and their importance for science, politics, law, justice and trust.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was present; null does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.rationale: The description centers epistemological interpretation and justification, not statistical inference techniques.

PHIL-312.name: American Philosophy
PHIL-312.description: Studies distinctive American philosophical traditions and their treatment of science, art, nature and democratic responsibility.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was present; null does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.rationale: Historical and social interpretation of ideas is the organizing purpose.

PHIL-313.name: Philosophy of Film
PHIL-313.description: Applies philosophical, aesthetic and psychoanalytic approaches to film interpretation, images, ideology and realism.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was present; null does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.rationale: Film is interpreted as culture and representation; no production-skills curriculum is described.

PHIL-314.name: Philosophy of Perception
PHIL-314.description: Examines sensory access to reality through philosophy and cognitive-science evidence, including cultural contexts, illusion and aesthetics.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was present; null does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.rationale: The course uses cognitive-science research to investigate conceptual and sociocultural meanings of perception, rather than teaching laboratory or computational methods.

PHIL-315.name: Responsible Knowing
PHIL-315.description: Examines evidence, cognitive bias, social knowledge, research integrity and the relation of knowledge claims to ethical action.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was present; null does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.rationale: Critical reasoning and ethical evaluation of individual and institutional knowledge organize the course; quantitative-method instruction is not specified.

PHIL-316.name: Bioethics and Society
PHIL-316.description: Uses ethical principles and cases to study medical practice, biological research, consent, healthcare allocation and public-health issues.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was present; null does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.rationale: Medical and biological cases support normative ethical inquiry rather than clinical or biological technique.

PHIL-317.name: Renaissance Philosophy
PHIL-317.description: Examines Renaissance humanism and its changing interpretations of art, nature, religion, history and politics.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was present; null does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.rationale: The stated scope is historical philosophical and cultural interpretation.

PHIL-318.name: Philosophies of Love,Sex, and Gender
PHIL-318.description: Compares philosophical accounts of love, desire, sexuality, identity and gender norms across historical traditions.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was present; null does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.rationale: The course centers conceptual and cultural interpretation of human relationships.

PHIL-319.name: Philosophy of Punishment
PHIL-319.description: Evaluates theories and practices of punishment through ethical, legal and historical accounts of justice.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was present; null does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.rationale: Normative legal and ethical analysis is central.

PHIL-320.name: AI Ethics
PHIL-320.description: Applies ethical concepts and recognized AI principles to machine moral status, data ethics and human-like artificial systems.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was present; null does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.rationale: The course teaches ethical evaluation of AI, not AI algorithms or system construction.

PHIL-401.name: Great Thinkers
PHIL-401.description: Studies selected influential philosophers in depth and the enduring problems and solutions in their work.
PHIL-401.prerequisites: Prerequisites: Completion of one course in philosophy is required.
notes: Description permits one philosophy course OR instructor permission; formal prerequisite field states completion of one course. Both source statements retained; no automatic waiver is granted.
Actual card states Writing Intensive: General Education; this attribute is not a guarantee of a current-term offering.

category_review.rationale: Although thinkers vary, the defined scope remains historical philosophical interpretation.

PHIL-402.name: Philosophy of Science
PHIL-402.description: Examines scientific presuppositions, reasoning, reliability and relationships with society and human values.
PHIL-402.prerequisites: Prerequisites: Completion of one (1) course in philosophy (at the 200 level or higher) or a major in the College of Science or College of Health Science & Technology or PSYC-BS.
notes: Actual card states Writing Intensive: General Education; this attribute is not a guarantee of a current-term offering.

category_review.rationale: Science is the object of philosophical critique, not a laboratory-method or statistical-computation syllabus.

PHIL-403.name: Social and Political Philosophy
PHIL-403.description: Compares philosophical views of individuals, society and their relationships.
PHIL-403.prerequisites: Prerequisites: Completion of one (1) course in any of the following disciplines: PHIL, POLS, SOCI, or CRIM.
notes: Actual card states Writing Intensive: General Education; this attribute is not a guarantee of a current-term offering.

category_review.rationale: The explicit scope is social and political interpretation.

PHIL-406.name: Contemporary Philosophy
PHIL-406.description: Examines modern philosophical movements and their interactions with science, technology, politics and the arts since 1900.
PHIL-406.prerequisites: Prerequisites: Must have completed at least one PHIL course - 200 level or higher.
notes: Actual card states Writing Intensive: General Education; this attribute is not a guarantee of a current-term offering.
Actual card also states Writing Intensive: Program; host-degree applicability still follows its program rules.

category_review.rationale: The course studies ideas and their historical-social significance rather than constructing the technologies discussed.

PHIL-407.name: Philosophy of Action
PHIL-407.description: Studies intentional action, agency, freedom, free will and moral responsibility.
PHIL-407.prerequisites: Prerequisites: Completion of one course in philosophy is required.
notes: Actual card states Writing Intensive: General Education; this attribute is not a guarantee of a current-term offering.

category_review.rationale: Action theory is presented as conceptual and ethical inquiry, not reinforcement-learning or control methods.

PHIL-408.name: Critical Social Theory
PHIL-408.description: Studies cultural critique, ideology, alienation, authority, advertising, technology and the autonomy of art.
PHIL-408.prerequisites: Prerequisites: Completion of one course in philosophy is required.
notes: Actual card states Writing Intensive: General Education; this attribute is not a guarantee of a current-term offering.

category_review.rationale: The description centers philosophical and cultural interpretation, even where economic and psychoanalytic frameworks are used.

PHIL-409.name: Existentialism
PHIL-409.description: Examines existence, meaning, freedom and responsibility through major philosophical and literary traditions.
PHIL-409.prerequisites: Prerequisites: Completion of one course in philosophy is required.
notes: Actual card states Writing Intensive: General Education; this attribute is not a guarantee of a current-term offering.

category_review.rationale: Human experience and ethical meaning are the stated subject.

PHIL-411.name: Metaphysics
PHIL-411.description: Examines major philosophical accounts of being, reality, time, causation, necessity, chance and value.
PHIL-411.prerequisites: Prerequisites: Must have completed at least one PHIL course - 200 level or higher.
notes: Actual card states Writing Intensive: General Education; this attribute is not a guarantee of a current-term offering.

category_review.rationale: These are conceptual questions in the history of philosophy; formal mathematical or physical-model methods are not described.

PHIL-412.name: Nineteenth Century Philosophy
PHIL-412.description: Surveys nineteenth-century philosophical and cultural movements, from idealism and Marxism to pragmatism and aesthetics.
PHIL-412.prerequisites: Prerequisites: Must have completed at least one PHIL course - 200 level or higher.
notes: Actual card states Writing Intensive: General Education; this attribute is not a guarantee of a current-term offering.

category_review.rationale: The organizing purpose is historical interpretation of ideas, not domain scientific practice.

PHIL-415.name: Ethical Theory
PHIL-415.description: Examines the theoretical commitments behind moral judgments, moral facts, actions and conceptions of a good life.
PHIL-415.prerequisites: Prerequisites: Completion of one course in philosophy is required.
notes: Actual card states Writing Intensive: General Education; this attribute is not a guarantee of a current-term offering.

category_review.rationale: The defined scope remains normative ethical inquiry despite a variable thinker or approach.

PHIL-416.name: Seminar in Philosophy
PHIL-416.description: Explores an instructor-selected philosophical research topic in a small discussion seminar open to majors and non-majors.
PHIL-416.prerequisites: Prerequisites: Completion of two (2) courses in philosophy is required.
notes: Open to majors and non-majors and may be retaken for credit; no additional repeat limit is supplied in this card.
Actual card states Writing Intensive: General Education; this attribute is not a guarantee of a current-term offering.
Actual card also states Writing Intensive: Program; host-degree applicability still follows its program rules.

category_review.rationale: The actual card leaves its substantive research topic unspecified; a particular subject category cannot be established.

PHIL-449.name: Topics in Philosophy
PHIL-449.description: Examines issues in a philosophical area not otherwise covered; the particular topic is unspecified.
PHIL-449.prerequisites: Prerequisites: Completion of one course in philosophy is required.
notes: Actual card states Writing Intensive: General Education; this attribute is not a guarantee of a current-term offering.

category_review.rationale: The current card does not identify the actual offering topic, so classification remains source-inspected but unclassified.

PHIL-504.name: Philosophy of Mind
PHIL-504.description: Critically examines mind, consciousness, mental/physical relations, rationality and whether computers can think.
notes: Explicitly designed for undergraduate and graduate students; graduate students fulfill additional requirements. No separate prerequisite field appears.
No separate prerequisite field was present; null does not establish unrestricted enrollment.
Actual card states Writing Intensive: General Education; this attribute is not a guarantee of a current-term offering.

category_review.rationale: Computers and cognition are objects of conceptual analysis, not evidence of AI or neuroscience implementation instruction.

PHIL-102.name: Introduction to Moral Issues
PHIL-102.description: Examines everyday moral questions and practical issues such as law, responsibility, medical choices and treatment of animals.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was present; null does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.rationale: The stated focus is practical ethical analysis of individual and social life.

PHIL-103.name: Critical Thinking
PHIL-103.description: Teaches evaluation of reasons and evidence, argumentation and common errors in causal, statistical, moral and everyday reasoning.
notes: No separate prerequisite field was present; null does not establish unrestricted enrollment.

category_review.rationale: General critical argument and justified action organize the course; mention of statistical errors is not a statistical-method curriculum.

MGMT-340.name: Business Ethics and Corporate Social Responsibility
MGMT-340.description: Examines business ideologies, corporate responsibilities and managerial ethical leadership through governance, employee rights, marketing, safety and environmental cases.
MGMT-340.prerequisites: This class is restricted to undergraduate students with at least 2nd year standing.

category_review.rationale: The actual description explicitly examines ethical obligations and institutional values at macro and managerial levels; it does not promise business-operations methods.
